units.translation: Always indeed you are pitiless and full of boldness.
when the sea, in its midday resting-places, calm and windless, sleeps, having fallen.
the spirit of a windless calm
I made those who were foolish before to be wise.
But you, having stirred them up with childish barkings, will lead them. Thus Iacobsius for ἠπίοις [gentle].
The Nereids was the title of a play by Aeschylus (fr. 150-153).

This word is not found in the Persians: therefore Blomfield thought of Epicharmus' Persians in his note on v. 897. To me it seems more probable that there is an error in the name of the play, either by the scribe or by Athenaeus himself, which perhaps was Περραιβίσιν [in the Perrhaebian Women], as in the scholia on Hermogenes vol. 5 p. 486, where ὑπόξυλον [wooden] is cited from Aeschylus' Πέρσαις [Persians], Blomfield conjectured Περραιβίσι [in the Perrhaebian Women] (fr. 439) in his Preface to the Persians p. XXVIII.
Aeschylus (fr. 438) in the Persians called certain islands νηριτοτρόφους [nurturing nerites]. Thus I corrected what is read in the codex: τίς ἀνήρει τοὺς νήσους [who was destroying the islands].
the echo of the island rock
around the island that nourishes doves
when the enemies, having been destroyed from the ships, might escape to the island
and they encircled the whole island
the sea-girt island of Ajax holds the Persian things
and the islands that are sea-girt along the sea-washed headland
and she wanders, fasting, along the sandy shore
and with fasting, violent outrages of leaping, he came rushing
and the blasts coming from the Strymon, bringing evil leisure, fasting
the night-wandering toil from battle, fasting
old age and the fasting miseries
and upon those who have been orphaned, fasting hunger presses
On this kind of sacrifice, see Thes. vol. 5 p. 1505.
Passive νικῶμαι [I am conquered] I am inferior
νικῶμαι [I am conquered] I am conquered
It is more frequently construed with the dative.
whether the rush of the bow is victorious
and the first and the last runner wins
whether the opinion of friends will prevail to bring him back
let us know whether we are winning or being defeated
I judge that you are winning
I say that unjust things should not prevail by oaths
and the strife of good men, ours, prevails through all
so that this matter may turn out well for you
let not fear conquer your mind
and no one has ever seen Zeus being conquered
being conquered, they butted the hard earth, where with the verb κύρισσον [they butted] it would be more fitting to have πεπτωκότες [having fallen] or δεδουπότες [having fallen with a thud].
